question: Does the predeclared world-society null (every system crosses 90 at the level's cross-system median year) generate an upper-secondary >=90 crossing for a system that never crossed?
estimand: count of systems with a null-generated upper-secondary >=90 crossing but no observed crossing (predeclared rule incl. right-censored/absent)
threshold: the rival is DISTINGUISHED on the upper-secondary margin only if the null generates an upper-secondary >=90 crossing for >=1 system that never crossed; falsifier -> NOT DISTINGUISHED
label: derived
note: Predeclared rule: the rival is DISTINGUISHED on the upper-secondary margin only if the null generates an upper-secondary >=90 crossing for >=1 system that never crossed; falsifier -> NOT DISTINGUISHED. Null = each level crosses 90 at that level's cross-system median of band midpoints (dated non-censored crossings only; censored rows excluded and listed). Upper-secondary null year = 2011.5 from n=1 dated non-censored crossing (HKG); never-crossed systems at upper secondary = 4 (CHN, JPN, KHM, PHL); null false crossings = 4 incl. absent, of which 2 testable against a record reaching the null year (CHN, PHL). Across all four 90% levels the null falsely crosses 7 system-level cells (4 evidence-backed). Descriptive null-model scoring only; no direction claim; C1-C4 not reopened. Caveat: with one dated non-censored upper-secondary crossing the null is thin; data-absent (JPN) cases are data absence, not evidence of non-crossing.
